subject: physics
title: Nuclear equations
key_idea: A nuclear equation shows radioactive decay. The total mass number and the total atomic number must be the same on both sides. Alpha decay lowers the mass number by 4 and the atomic number by 2. Beta decay raises the atomic number by 1. Gamma emission changes neither.

blocks.text: A nuclear equation represents radioactive decay. Each nucleus or particle is written with its mass number at the top and its atomic number at the bottom.

items: The mass number is the number of protons plus neutrons.
The atomic number is the number of protons, which is the charge of the nucleus. It is also called the proton number.
A beta particle has almost no mass, so its mass number is 0. Its charge is -1.
Alpha is ⁴₂He. Beta is ⁰₋₁e. Gamma has no mass and no charge.
Mass number is at the top and atomic number is at the bottom.

sections.heading: How each type of decay changes the nucleus

blocks.text: Emitting radiation may change the mass and the charge of the nucleus. The changes depend on the type of radiation.

rows: Two protons and two neutrons leave the nucleus.
A neutron becomes a proton and an electron. The electron is emitted.
The nucleus loses energy as gamma radiation.

items: Alpha decay decreases both the mass and the charge of the nucleus.
Beta decay does not change the mass of the nucleus. It increases the charge of the nucleus.
A nucleus that has just decayed is often left with extra energy. It loses this as gamma radiation, and its mass and charge do not change.

diagram.alt: Pick a type of decay to see how the nucleus changes.

options.label: Alpha decay
results: Two protons and two neutrons are emitted as an alpha particle.

options.label: Beta decay (β⁻)
results: A neutron changes into a proton, and an electron is emitted.

options.label: Gamma emission
results: The nucleus loses energy as a gamma ray.

items: Alpha decay: mass number -4, atomic number -2.
Beta decay: mass number unchanged, atomic number +1.
Gamma emission changes neither number.

blocks.text: In a balanced nuclear equation, the numbers on the left equal the numbers on the right. Check the top numbers and the bottom numbers separately.

blocks.label: Mass number balance
blocks.formula: mass number before = mass numbers added together after
where: Mass numbers are the top numbers in the symbols.

blocks.label: Atomic number balance
blocks.formula: atomic number before = atomic numbers added together after
where: Atomic numbers are the bottom numbers in the symbols.

items.text: 210 = 210 + mass number, so the particle has mass number 0.
83 = 84 + atomic number, so the particle has atomic number -1.
Mass 0 and atomic number -1 is a beta particle, ⁰₋₁e.

blocks.text: An alpha decay example is uranium-238: ²³⁸₉₂U → ²³⁴₉₀Th + ⁴₂He. Check: 238 = 234 + 4 and 92 = 90 + 2.

diagram.alt: Calculate the mass number after alpha decay of uranium.
diagram.question: A uranium nucleus has atomic number 92 and mass number {A}. It emits an alpha particle. Calculate the mass number of the new nucleus.
working: Alpha particle: ⁴₂He, so the mass number falls by 4

items: Balance the top numbers, then balance the bottom numbers.
Use the numbers to find a missing particle.

checks.a: Mass number 230 - 4 = 226. Atomic number 92 - 2 = 90. The product is ²²⁶₉₀Th.

checks.q: Describe the effect of beta emission on the mass number and charge of a nucleus.
checks.a: The mass number stays the same. The charge increases by 1, because a neutron becomes a proton.

checks.q: A nucleus emits an alpha particle, then two beta particles. How does its atomic number change overall?
checks.a: Alpha decreases it by 2. Each beta increases it by 1, so +2 in all. The atomic number is the same as at the start.

worked_example.question:
A polonium (Po) nucleus decays by emitting an alpha particle and forming a lead (Pb) nucleus.
Po → Pb + α
The lead nucleus then decays by emitting a beta particle and forms a bismuth (Bi) nucleus.
Pb → Bi + β
The bismuth nucleus then decays by emitting a beta particle and forms a polonium nucleus.
Bi → Po + β

Explain how these three decays result in a nucleus of the original element, polonium.
answer_points: One alpha decay would decrease the proton number by 2.
Two beta decays would increase the proton number by 2.
So the proton (atomic) number of the final nucleus is the same as that of the original nucleus.
worked_example.tip: The third mark is only given if the first two are scored.

blocks.text: A nucleus can also decay by emitting a positron, written ⁰₊₁e. This is beta-plus (β⁺) decay.

items: In β⁺ decay a proton becomes a neutron plus a positron.
The mass number stays the same and the atomic number decreases by 1.
In neutron emission the nucleus loses a neutron. The mass number decreases by 1 and the atomic number stays the same.

worked_example.question: Describe what happens in the nucleus of an atom when a positron is emitted.
worked_example.tip: Writing p → n scores both marks. If no other mark is scored, the atomic number decreasing by one, the mass number staying the same or the charge of the nucleus reducing by one earns 1 mark.

items: A neutron is written ¹₀n. It has mass number 1 and atomic number 0.
When a nucleus emits a neutron its mass number falls by 1 and its atomic number stays the same.

worked_example.question:
A nuclear reactor needs neutrons to start a nuclear fission reaction.

A plutonium nucleus (Pu) decays into a uranium nucleus (U) and an alpha particle (⁴₂He).

The alpha particle then joins with a beryllium nucleus (Be) to produce a carbon nucleus (C) and a neutron (n).

Complete the equations.

²³⁸₉₄Pu → ______U + ⁴₂He

⁹₄Be + ⁴₂He → ¹²₆C + ______n
answer_points: ²³⁸₉₄Pu → ²³⁴₉₂U + ⁴₂He: the correct mass number for U is 234.
The correct atomic number for U is 92.
⁹₄Be + ⁴₂He → ¹²₆C + ¹₀n: the correct mass number and atomic number for the neutron, 1 and 0.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each of the three numbers or pairs of numbers.

worked_example.question:
Sodium-24 is an isotope of sodium (Na) that has a proton number of 11 and a nucleon number of 24.

Sodium-24 decays by emission of a beta-particle to form an isotope of magnesium (Mg).

Use nuclide notation to write down the nuclide equation for this decay.

items: In alpha decay and in beta decay the nucleus changes into the nucleus of a different element, because its proton number changes.
(Supplement) Decay makes an unstable nucleus more stable. It reduces the number of excess neutrons or the extra energy in the nucleus.
(Supplement) In beta emission a neutron changes into a proton and an electron: n → p + e⁻. The electron is emitted as the beta particle.

worked_example.question:
Thorium-232 (²³²₉₀Th) decays by a sequence of alpha decays and beta decays to form radon-220 (²²⁰₈₆Rn).

The incomplete nuclear decay equation summarises the decay sequence:

²³²₉₀Th → ²²⁰₈₆Rn + ___ ⁴₂α + ___ ⁰₋₁β

Calculate the number of alpha particles and the number of beta particles emitted in this decay sequence.
answer_points: Balance the mass numbers: 232 - 220 = 12, and 12 ÷ 4 gives 3 alpha particles.
Balance the atomic numbers: 90 = 86 + (3 × 2) + (number of betas × -1).
Number of alpha particles = 3 and number of beta particles = 2.

blocks.text: Neutron emission also changes the nucleus. The mass number falls by 1 and the atomic number stays the same, because a neutron has mass number 1 and no charge. The symbol for a neutron is ¹₀n.
